nodes.description: Current contract owner; assigned msg.sender in the Owned constructor, used in the onlyOwner modifier, and reassigned in acceptOwnership.
Pending owner set by transferOwnership and consumed/zeroed by acceptOwnership.
Token symbol string, set to 'NBL' in the constructor.
Token name string, set to 'NebuliToken' in the constructor.
Token decimals, fixed to 18 in the constructor.
Total token supply, minted to the deployer address in the constructor and read by totalSupply().
Mapping of token holder balances; mutated by transfer and transferFrom, read by balanceOf and totalSupply.
Nested mapping of owner->spender allowances; written by approve/approveAndCall and decremented in transferFrom.
Placeholder guard for safeAdd; overflow-checked addition helper used by transfer and transferFrom.
Underflow-checked subtraction helper (require(b <= a)) used by transfer, transferFrom and allowance accounting.
Overflow-checked multiplication helper.
Division helper with divide-by-zero guard.
Owned constructor that sets owner to msg.sender.
onlyOwner function that stages a new owner in newOwner.
Two-step ownership acceptance; requires msg.sender == newOwner then moves owner to newOwner and clears newOwner.
Token constructor that sets metadata, mints the full supply to a hardcoded address and emits Transfer.
Returns _totalSupply minus balances[address(0)] using an unchecked subtraction.
Returns the balance of a token owner.
Transfers tokens from msg.sender to a recipient, updating balances via safeSub/safeAdd.
Sets allowed[msg.sender][spender] = tokens and emits Approval.
Moves tokens from 'from' to 'to' and decrements the caller's allowance; allowance decrement is bound by safeSub.
Returns the remaining allowance for a spender.
Sets allowance then invokes an untrusted spender contract via receiveApproval, creating a reentrancy surface.
Payable fallback function that unconditionally reverts.
onlyOwner function that performs an arbitrary external ERC20 transfer call to an owner-supplied token address.
Caller-supplied address used for ownership, authorization checks and balance/allowance ownership.
External call ApproveAndCallFallBack(spender).receiveApproval(...) to an attacker-controlled contract, enabling reentrancy.
External call ERC20Interface(tokenAddress).transfer(owner, tokens) to an arbitrary, potentially malicious token contract.

edges.reason: transfer reads and writes the balances mapping for msg.sender and the recipient.
transferFrom mutates balances[from] and balances[to].
transferFrom decrements allowed[from][msg.sender].
approve writes allowed[msg.sender][spender].
approveAndCall writes allowed[msg.sender][spender] before the external call.
approveAndCall transfers control to an attacker-controlled spender contract, which can re-enter token functions.
transferAnyERC20Token performs an external call on an owner-supplied contract address that can re-enter.
The untrusted receiveApproval callback can re-enter approve/transferFrom and manipulate the allowed mapping.
Owner address is derived directly from the untrusted msg.sender in the Owned constructor.
transferOwnership is gated by require(msg.sender == owner) in the onlyOwner modifier.
acceptOwnership authorizes the state change with require(msg.sender == newOwner).
transferAnyERC20Token is restricted to the owner via the onlyOwner modifier.
transfer uses msg.sender as the debited account.
approve uses msg.sender as the allowance owner.
transferFrom uses msg.sender as the spender whose allowance is deducted.
approveAndCall uses msg.sender as allowance owner and forwards it to the untrusted contract.
transferOwnership writes the pending owner into newOwner.
acceptOwnership reads and then clears newOwner.
acceptOwnership reassigns ownership; the authorization relies on the untrusted msg.sender matching newOwner.
totalSupply performs an unchecked subtraction on _totalSupply with no SafeMath guard.
totalSupply subtracts balances[address(0)], which is an unchecked read of a mutable balance.
The recipient address parameter flows into the balances credit in transfer.
The amount parameter flows into the safeSub/safeAdd balance updates in transfer.
The source address parameter flows into balances[from] and allowed[from][...] updates.
The recipient address parameter flows into the balances credit in transferFrom.
The amount parameter flows into the balance and allowance decrements in transferFrom.
The spender parameter is used both as allowance key and as the callee of the untrusted external call.
The token amount parameter flows into the allowance write and the external call arguments.
The arbitrary bytes parameter is forwarded verbatim into the untrusted callback.
The token address parameter determines the target of the external ERC20 call.
The token amount parameter is forwarded into the external ERC20 transfer.
The candidate owner parameter is stored into newOwner by transferOwnership.

Arbitrary data forwarded directly into the untrusted external call.
